transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Lately I can’t seem to keep my actions in order at work. I start doing things that don’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing and everything just turns into a mess.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'things that don’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing' and if you've been feeling restless or having trouble waiting for your turn in situations?

On the warehouse floor, I'll suddenly stop in the middle of moving a pallet to hold the jack in a weird way, or start re-stacking boxes that are already fine. I don't really feel restless or have trouble waiting my turn, it's just that I do these strange actions and pace around without really knowing why.
Do you find yourself repeating these actions or behaviors outside of work, such as at home or during your free time?

Yes, it's definitely happening outside of work too, like at home and at church. My family and my pastor have noticed that I've been acting really disorganized and out of step lately. Because of that, people have started avoiding putting me in charge of things since I just can't follow through like I used to.
Can you tell me if you've been having any repetitive thoughts or urges to perform specific rituals or behaviors that you feel compelled to do, even if they don't make sense to you?

No, I don't really experience repetitive thoughts or feel compelled by specific urges to do rituals. It's more that I just find myself doing strange things, like re-stacking boxes or pacing, without really knowing why I'm doing them.
Do you feel like you're doing these strange actions on purpose, even if you're not sure why, or do you feel like they're happening without you really being in control of them?

No, I don't really do them on purpose. I'll just suddenly find myself stopping in the middle of a task, pacing, waving my hands, or making faces without really knowing why. Even when my supervisor tells me to stop, it's really hard for me to get back on track.

Have you noticed any significant difficulty in paying attention to details, making careless mistakes, or avoiding tasks that require mental effort, which might be contributing to the disorganization and strange actions you've described?

I haven't really noticed having trouble with careless mistakes or trying to avoid hard tasks. It feels more like my mind just gets jumbled up and I lose track of my actions, rather than me trying to avoid the work.

Have you ever found yourself blurting out answers before questions have been completed, interrupting others, or intruding on conversations, which might be related to the impulsive actions you've been experiencing?

No, I don't really find myself interrupting people or blurting out answers. My main difficulty is that once I'm already in a conversation or trying to work, I just completely lose track of my own thoughts and actions.

Have you experienced any episodes of sudden, brief, involuntary movements or vocalizations, such as twitching, grimacing, or making odd sounds, which might be related to your strange actions and disorganization?

I don't think I make odd sounds or have sudden twitches, but I definitely make strange faces and wave my hands around. It's like these things just happen when I'm on the floor, and I really can't explain why I'm doing them.
Can you tell me at what age you first started noticing these strange behaviors and if they have been present since childhood, or if they started more recently?

No, they haven't been around since childhood; this all started pretty recently. I'm 20 years old now, and these problems began about a year ago after I left community college to work full-time. The really strange actions and confused way of talking have been a constant issue for about the last six months.

You mentioned that these behaviors started about a year ago, after leaving community college. Can you tell me if there were any significant stressors, changes, or events in your life around that time that might have triggered the onset of these symptoms?

Leaving community college was a major transition and a huge adjustment for me. Moving from the predictable structure of school and part-time shifts into full-time warehouse work with rotating schedules and heavier responsibilities was incredibly stressful. That major shift is really when everything started falling apart and these difficulties began.

Can you describe any significant developmental delays or difficulties you experienced during childhood, such as problems with speech, motor skills, or social interactions, that might help clarify the origin of your current symptoms?

I don't recall having any developmental delays, speech issues, or major difficulties during my childhood. Everything was pretty normal for me growing up. These problems only really started recently after I left college.

You mentioned that these behaviors started about a year ago, but can you tell me if you've noticed any periods where these symptoms have significantly improved or worsened, or if they've remained relatively consistent over the past year?

The general decline started about a year ago when I transitioned to full-time work, but the strange actions and confused talking have been a constant, steady problem for the last six months. They haven't really improved or fluctuated at all during this time. It has just been a persistent struggle every single day.

You mentioned that these behaviors started recently, but can you confirm if you had any symptoms of autism spectrum disorder, such as difficulties with social interactions or restricted interests, during your childhood or adolescence that may not have been severe enough to cause significant impairment at the time?
I don't think I had those kinds of problems growing up. I did fine with social interactions and enjoyed normal hobbies like fishing and woodworking without any issues back then.

Can you describe any instances where you've had difficulty with coordination or balance, such as stumbling, tripping, or having trouble with fine motor tasks like writing or using tools, in addition to the strange actions and pacing you've mentioned?

No, I haven't really had any issues with my balance, stumbling, or using tools and writing. It's not a coordination problem; it's more about those weird postures, pacing, and actions I described where I just stop and do things that don't make sense.

Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning as a result of these strange actions and behaviors, and if so, can you describe how they have impacted your daily life and relationships?

Yes, these struggles have had a massive impact on my life. Because I get so mixed up, my boss wrote me up for poor performance and cut my hours back at the warehouse. Even at home and at church, people have stopped putting me in charge of things because I can't seem to follow through like I used to.
Have you experienced any episodes of sudden, brief, involuntary vocalizations or movements, such as tics, that might be related to your strange actions and disorganization?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like tics or involuntary vocalizations. The strange movements I do, like pacing or holding the pallet jack weirdly, don't feel like sudden twitches or anything like that.

Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any episodes of sudden, brief, involuntary movements or vocalizations, such as twitching, grimacing, or making odd sounds, that might be related to your strange actions and disorganization, and if so, have you noticed any triggers or patterns to when these episodes occur?

I do make strange faces like grimacing, wave my hands around, and sometimes freeze in odd positions at work without really knowing why. I don't experience any sudden twitches or make odd sounds, and there are no specific triggers other than these things just happening while I'm trying to work.
Can you describe in more detail the strange faces, hand waving, and freezing in odd positions you experience, and whether these movements are repetitive, rhythmic, or seem to serve any purpose?

When I'm working, I'll suddenly stop in the middle of moving a pallet and just stand there holding the jack in an odd way, or pace up and down the aisle waving my hands and making faces. These actions don't serve any purpose at all, and I honestly don't know why I do them. I even keep doing them when my supervisor tells me to knock it off and get back to the actual job.

You mentioned that these behaviors started around the time you transitioned to full-time work, but can you confirm if you had any subtle signs or traits during adolescence that might have been indicative of a neurodevelopmental disorder, even if they didn't cause significant problems at the time?

I don't think I had any signs or traits like that when I was a teenager. In fact, I used to be very organized and detailed back then, especially when I was planning fishing trips or working on my woodworking projects.

Can you clarify if you experienced any subtle difficulties with social interactions, flexibility, or repetitive behaviors during adolescence that may have been overlooked or not caused significant problems at the time, which could help differentiate between the potential diagnoses?
I don't really recall having those kinds of social or behavioral difficulties during adolescence. Back then, I managed my school and my hobbies like woodworking and fishing just fine.
Can you tell me if the strange faces, hand waving, or freezing in odd positions you experience are always the same, or if they vary from one episode to another?
I'm not really sure if they are always the same or if they change. I haven't really thought about it because I usually just find myself doing them without even realizing why.
Can you describe if the strange actions, like making faces or waving your hands, happen in a specific pattern or sequence, or if they seem completely random and unpredictable?

No, they don't follow any pattern or sequence at all. They seem completely random and just happen out of nowhere, without me really knowing why. It's totally unpredictable, even when I'm right in the middle of trying to focus on my work.
Can you tell me if you've ever felt like you're trying to relieve anxiety or tension by performing these strange actions, or if they seem to be completely unrelated to any emotional state you're in?

No, they don't feel like they are done to relieve any anxiety or tension. They just seem to happen out of nowhere, and I really don't know why I'm doing them. It's just very confusing because there doesn't seem to be any emotional reason or feeling behind it.

Can you tell me if you've noticed that these strange actions, like making faces or waving your hands, are self-soothing or seem to be done for their own sake, even if they don't make sense to you or others?

Yes, I do make those movements like waving my hands and making faces, but I don't really know why I'm doing them. They don't feel like they are meant to calm me down or soothe me, and they don't serve any specific purpose. They just happen without any clear reason.

Can you tell me if you've ever felt like these strange actions, such as waving your hands or making faces, are something you feel compelled to do, even if they don't make sense to you, and if stopping them would cause you significant distress?

No, I don't feel any kind of compulsion to do them, and stopping wouldn't cause me any distress or anxiety. I just find myself making faces or waving my hands spontaneously, without really knowing why I'm doing it. It's not like I have an urge I need to satisfy; they just happen.

It feels very hard to control once it starts, and I can't just stop myself. I don't really know why I'm pacing, waving my hands, or holding the jack in a weird way, and even when my supervisor tells me to knock it off, I find it really difficult to just snap out of it.
Have you ever noticed any premonitory urges, which are feelings or sensations that you get right before you make one of these strange faces, wave your hands, or exhibit any other unusual behavior?
I do make those faces and wave my hands, but I don't experience any warning sensations or urges beforehand. I just suddenly find myself doing these things without really knowing why.

Do you feel like you're aware of what's happening while you're making these strange faces or exhibiting the other unusual behaviors, or does it feel like you're not fully aware of your actions until after they've happened?

Yes, I'm aware of what I'm doing while it's happening—for instance, I can hear my supervisor telling me to knock it off right in the moment. But I just don't know *why* I'm doing it. These actions, like pacing, waving my hands, or making faces, just happen without any clear reason or purpose, which leaves me feeling really confused.

Can you describe if there's a moment, right as you're about to do one of these strange actions, where you feel like you could still choose not to do it, or if it feels completely outside of your control from the very start?

I'm not quite sure how to describe it, because I don't really feel a moment where I'm deciding to do it. These actions usually just happen suddenly without me thinking about them or planning them beforehand.

Do you think that if you were in a situation where it was extremely important to not make these strange faces or exhibit these behaviors, such as in a job interview or a very formal setting, you would be able to control yourself and not do them?

No, I don't think I would be able to control it even if it was really important, because these behaviors like making faces, pacing, or freezing just happen without me knowing why. Even when my supervisor tells me to stop on the spot I can't seem to help it, and I've already had trouble behaving appropriately in formal settings like church.
